 This Mfa Is Filed U/S.173(1) Of Mv Act Against The
Judgment And Award Dated 29.06.2018 Passed In Mvc
No.363/2016 On The File Of The Senior Civil Judge,
Kundapura And Member, Additional Mact, Kundapura,
Allowing The Claim Petition For Compensation And
Seeking Enhancement Of Compensation.

This Appeal, Coming On For Orders, This Day, The
Court Delivered The Following:
 Judgment

1. Aggrieved by the judgment and award dated 29.06.2018 passed in MVC No.363/2016 by the Court of the Senior Civil Judge and Additional MACT, Kundapura (for short 'the Tribunal'), the petitioner therein has preferred this appeal.
2. For the sake of convenience, the parties are referred to herein as per their status before the Tribunal.

3. Brief facts of the case are as follows:
The petitioner on 23.10.2015 was traveling in a Car bearing Reg.No.KA-05/MQ-7522.

When the Car reached near Alkodu, Nagodi, Nittur Village, Nagara, Hosanagara taluk, the driver of the Car lost control of the same and dashed against a tree, because of which, the petitioner NC: 2023:KHC:29138 sustained fracture of right leg superior pubic rami and fracture of left leg sacral ALA and has suffered 9% disability to the whole body.
The Tribunal has awarded a compensation of Rs.2,30,677/- along with interest at 6% p.a. from the date of accident till the date of realization.
Not satisfied by the same, the present appeal is filed by the petitioner.
4. Admittedly the petitioner has suffered 9% whole body disability due to the accident.
The Car was duly insured with respondent No.2-Insurance Company at the time of accident.
The liability of the insurance company is not in dispute.
5. The petitioner has failed to prove her income before the Tribunal.
Hence, her income is determined as per the chart prepared by the Karnataka State Legal Services Authority in consultation with Insurance Companies which will be Rs.9,000/- per month.

Taking the income of the petitioner at Rs.9,000/- per month, her age being 29 years at the time of accident, the multiplier of '17' is applicable and the disability to the whole body at 9%, the petitioner would be entitled to a sum of Rs.1,65,240/- (9,000/-x12x17x9%) towards 'loss of future income'.

7. Towards medical expenses based on actual bills, a sum of Rs.23,047/- is awarded.

Towards diet,
conveyance and attendance charges a sum of Rs.20,000/- is awarded.
Towards loss of amenities a sum of Rs.20,000/- is awarded.
Given the nature of injuries, I deem the same to be appropriate.
8. Towards pain and suffering a sum of Rs.20,000/- is awarded.
Given the fact that there are two fractures, I deem it appropriate to enhance it to Rs.40,000/-.
9. Towards loss of income during laid up period, a sum of Rs.19,110/- is awarded.
Given the nature of injuries, three months is considered as the laid up period and NC: 2023:KHC:29138 taking the income at Rs.9,000/- per month
, a sum of Rs.27,000/- is hereby awarded.

10. Thus, the petitioner is entitled to a total compensation of Rs.2,95,287/- as against Rs,2,30.677/-
awarded by the Tribunal.

Accordingly, the petitioner is entitled to an enhanced compensation of Rs.64,610/- (Rs.2,95,287/- minus Rs.2,30,677/-).
11.
Given the bank rate of interest, I deem it appropriate to award interest at the rate of 6% p.a. on the enhanced compensation from the date of petition till realization.
